function: Joint NOMA power allocation (agent 1) and IRS mirror roll/yaw orientation (agent 2), maximizing sum energy efficiency times Jain fairness (p. 6-7).
system: Indoor 5x5x3 m room, 4 ceiling LED APs, K=5 users (Table I lists 8) with angle-diversity receivers, 7x7 reflecting mirror-array IRS, visible light, 20 MHz (p. 9-10).
method: Two-agent DDPG-style actor-critic with fully connected networks, centralized training and decentralized execution; reinforcement learning, trained offline (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Own simulator: Lambertian VLC LoS channel [36] plus mirror-array NLoS model [5], random-waypoint user mobility; no dataset or measurement (p. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Training: 2,000 episodes of 100 slots under random-waypoint mobility. Testing: new random trajectories of the same model; sweeps of power, mirrors, users, Rmin (p. 10-12).
baselines: Non-learned: SCA, exhaustive search, fixed-power allocation. Learned: standard DDPG and DQN; DDPG with random-orientation IRS or without IRS; OMA variant of proposed (p. 11-13).
metrics: Sum energy efficiency, sum rate, Jain fairness index, mean reward, convergence episodes, training time per episode, inference time per slot (p. 11-13).
complexity: Big-O of actor and critic networks, e.g. O((2K+2M)K) (p. 9); 0.34 s per training episode, 0.51 ms inference per slot, SCA 96.7 s (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 10: "computed in real-time using the Lambertian VLC channel model"; custom simulator, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "the learned policies generalize to new random trajectory realizations"; same simulator and mobility model, and the paper never states a train-on-one-setting, test-on-another for mirrors (Fig. 7) or users (Fig. 8).
q3_support: p. 11: "16% improvement over the SCA algorithm (8.2 Mb/Joule)" and "34% better than DDPG (7.1 Mb/Joule) and 32% better than DQN (7.2 Mb/Joule)", on sum energy efficiency.
q4_support: p. 9: "the complexity of the actor-network is O((2K + 2M ) × K)"; p. 11: "forward passes requiring only 0.51 milliseconds per time slot".
q5_support: p. 10: "trained offline in a simulated VLC environment"; no code or data link and no public dataset or measured data is given.
notes: The IRS is an optical mirror array (passive rotatable mirrors) in an indoor NOMA-VLC downlink, not an RF metasurface: scope for the reviewer to confirm. Area 3 because agent 2 sets the IRS mirror orientation and agent 1 the NOMA power allocation (p. 6). Table I lists 8 users while the text uses K=5 (p. 9-10). The OMA curve of Fig. 5 is the proposed algorithm applied to OMA, so it is not counted as a baseline (p. 11). q2: state and action dimensions depend on K and M (p. 9), and the paper does not say whether Figs. 7-8 reuse trained agents. q1: the Lambertian VLC channel [36] is a textbook model, not a standardized one (p. 4).
